subject.title: Duplicate slug rows after squat removal break publish/scan pipeline — new versions never go live (shieldcortex stuck at 4.47.12)

question: Should maintainers authorize an incident-specific production reconciliation for the duplicate `shieldcortex` records and a bounded shared slug-lookup hardening pass before unblocking the pending version?
rationale: The source repair can be scoped, but identifying the canonical production row and performing destructive or state-moving reconciliation requires operator access and ownership judgment that automated issue repair should not infer.

options.title: Authorize reconciliation and hardening
options.body: Select the canonical active `shieldcortex` record, reconcile the duplicate row and dependent state, then land bounded duplicate-safe slug resolution with real Convex proof.

options.title: Perform data repair only
options.body: Unblock the pending version through an audited one-time reconciliation, while tracking shared lookup hardening separately if no other active consumer is affected.

options.title: Pause for an incident audit
options.body: Keep the publish blocked until maintainers confirm every affected data relation and the intended historical retention policy.

recommendation.title: Authorize reconciliation and hardening
recommendation.body: Select the canonical active `shieldcortex` record, reconcile the duplicate row and dependent state, then land bounded duplicate-safe slug resolution with real Convex proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent merged work establishes the repository’s bounded, fail-closed duplicate-row reconciliation pattern.
